descriptionChirho: The primary postpositive conjunction serving as an adversative ('but, however'), continuative ('and, now'), or transitional marker ('then') that connects clauses and advances narrative. This is by far the dominant usage across all 2,806 occurrences in the NT. Multilingual glosses show the dual adversative-connective function: Spanish 'pero' (adversative) and implicit connective, Arabic 'وَ' (connective), Hindi 'और' (and) / 'परन्तु' (but), Korean '그런데' (but/now) / '그러나' (however), Swahili 'lakini' (but) / 'na' (and). The particle is so frequent and semantically light that many languages leave it untranslated or render it as simple coordination.

A rare partitive or distributive use of δέ where the conjunction introduces a contrasting subgroup ('but others,' 'some... but others'), functioning almost pronominally to mark a distinct party within a larger set. This usage is attested only 3 times and is semantically distinct from the standard connective. Multilingual evidence highlights the partitive nuance: Spanish 'otros' (others), Arabic 'وَبَعضَهُم' (and some of them), Hindi 'पर' (but/on the other hand), Korean '또–한편으로는' (on yet another hand), Swahili 'wengine' (others). The translation signatures diverge sharply from the main sense, using substantival or pronominal glosses rather than simple conjunctions.
